reviews.text: The place is strict with the admission timing. You will not be allowed to enter if you miss your slot. If you arrive early, join the snaking queue until the a lot starts. Takes about 20-30min before I can get in. Place is way overcrowded, as it’s jn the city and it’s FREE! Book early to get the ticket. Many of the exhibits in the museum are replicas. Make your own decision if you want to visit.

One of the most historic and beautiful museums I have ever set foot on in my life. The exterior and interior are equally beautiful, both showing the great historical culture of Xi-an and Chinese history. There are two floors and many rooms in the museum to store these delicate artifacts in the museum, each of these artifacts is magnificent, vibrating an ancient aroma that can bring the visitors to Ancient China, seeing how they lived and what they used back then. Through this museum, you can as if retrieve your footsteps and view the development of China and see its history with your own eyes, immensely increasing your own historical knowledge about the place. What a beautiful museum! Also the sensation of just seeing the photos online in comparison to seeing them in person are completely different.

Great collections of few dynasties over thousands years ago! A little crowded to really appreciate these amazing collections. Definitely worth the visit but make sure to pre-booked the ticket online prior to avoid disappointment.
Virtually impossible to get in for a foreigner. Wechat reservation only in Chinese and days ahead possible. I am sure it's a great museum, which I will never see I my life.

It is a great museum charting the history of Xi'An. Lots to see and it is free to enter if you are lucky enough to get one of the 12000 tickets issued every day. I have only rated 3 stars for the following reasons: The wait in line is around 1 and a half hours, if you get there early, if you arrive later in the day it can be much longer. The temperature in Xi'An is around 38 degrees c in the afternoon and it is not until you get closer to the museum entrance that some shade is provided, so bear that in mind when you visit. The museum was severely overcrowded, and this unfortunately spoilt the experience as viewing the displays was very difficult due to the sheer amount of people in the museum. There was a lot of pushing and shoving due to the lack of space around the exhibits. The museum staff were friendly and helpful.

One of the best museum that I have visited in my life, we have booked the ticket in advance from trip.com it’s easy just passport to show. A lot of history showcasing, for me it’s good to visit before going to Emperor Qinshihuang’s mausoleum, you will understand piece by piece.
This is a must-visit place in Xi An. It's free, but make sure to book your ticket in advance. Try to avoid the holiday season or weekends.

You have to pre book ticket, and you should chose the earliest time, I dont know if they clean everyday but I go on Tuesday 12h30 and the glass is like full of fingerprints you can hardly see thing anymore And they are not foreigners friendly you can not have ticket if you are just go to the ticket counter and book it sucks The exhibition is ok

Brilliant museum but the queue to get in where out of control took almost 2 hours. Wouldn't recommend in the peak of heat or if you can try book tickets. Otherwise this museum is brilliant and well worth going.

Didn’t get to visit because near impossible for a foreigner to get the tickets without a valid Chinese ID. You can book a tour like I did but operator cancelled on me because they fail to secure tickets for us too. Quick check with the local Chinese travellers on another tour revealed the same so be assured it’s not a China vs Foreigner phenomenon.

A great place to see a lot of Tang dynasty art and murals. It was pretty packed and stuffy when we went (prior to COVID), and it wasn't the most peaceful museum experience, with people yelling, tour groups pushing and it just gave an overall chaotic experience to the museum. Our main reason for coming here was to see the Tang dynasty murals that are housed here. This is a separate entrance fee ($35 USD at the time) and you're required to wear shoe coverings and no pictures are allowed. This exhibit was extraordinarily quiet and peaceful and the murals are displayed in a captivating and powerful way, reminiscent of their original home in the tombs. Note that although some scrolls in this exhibit portray themselves to be authentic, many of them are actually replicas, as the actual scrolls are in museums abroad. Note: Visited prior to COVID, so things may be different.

This is a great museum that focuses on the region and its role in the history of China over the past ~10000 years. I was amazed by just how important it has been. Very good layout and has a fair amount of English content descriptions. A visit is a great compliment to the much more famous terra cotta soldiers/emperor"s burial sites. Tickets are required and if you are a senior they are free, but a bit complicated to get--several lines and lines may be long. A guide can be useful but seems audio guides only in Chinese.

A must visit museum in Xi'an. It is the largest museum in Xi'an describing the history from the Chin dynasty to the Qing dynasty. By far the most informative museum in Xi'an. You can skip other museums if you have covered this one. Pro tip: 1) This museum gives online free tickets (reserved until 2500 entries per day) on their website. Check one week before your intended plan of visit day. 0therwsie the free tickets will run out of stock. 2) If you miss the online tickets, you could still buy the usual tickets (30 CNY) from their website and book the time slot. This is absolutely necessary. Do not just turn up to buy the tickets on the spot. You won't get any! 3) For the special exhibition of the mural paintings from the Tang dynasty (270 CNY), I would suggest to give it a skip if you are not a history buff. For a usual person, it is not that interesting as those are only the paintings on the stone wall. If you are a history expert, then you may be interested in it.

A world-class museum with multiple pieces at the national treasure level (highest possible). Hint: an ancient piece with scripts on it is likely to be a national treasure. Must see if you are visiting Xi'an. Free admissions. The museum limits 5000 visitors in the morning and another 5000 in the afternoon. Arrive early to get free tickets. Passport or ID is needed. To get the best of it, hire a tour guide (right past entrance) or rent a guide machine (left past entrance)

I cannot give a review of the museum as it’s impossible for foreigners or anyone without WeChat to get in. You need to book in advance but this is only possible through WeChat. I went to the ticket office only to be told it was sold out for 3 days. You must book in advance and you must have WeChat set up which is difficult for foreigners. Even with tickets people were queuing down the street, it appears to be a very busy and crowded museum, even on weekdays.

Visiting the museum was one of the original plans in my Xi’an trip. But it was the worst experience. Tourists need to pay money buying tickets to enter most scenery places in Xi’an. But the museum is an exception. You had to line to get free tickets. At the end I didn’t make it, although it was free. The lining situation was awful. The staffs of the museum didn’t make the waiting line clear. Visitors wanted to get free tickets quickly. Some cut in line and didn’t follow rules. Maybe they were not intended to do that. After staying in line about 40 minutes, I felt angry and disappointed then left. It wasted my time. The best way to enjoy the exhibitions in the museum is to make a reservation online in advance.
I'm here now... 291118. No queue at ticket counter. Nice cooling weather. Ticket is free but need your passport for the tickets.
Great museum with beautiful artifacts. Very crowded. The most important pieces are in the centre of the room. I wished there were more detailed description in English or an English speaking docents.
A famous museum with an impressive collection. It’s just very crowded with a lot of tourist guides and big groups. And I was there at an off-peak season.
A nice museum with lots of antiques and cultural relics from the ancient days.. great place to learn the historical culture..
An interesting museum specially focus two chinese greatest dynasties of Qing and Tang. Online booking as a good option avoid long queue for entrance.
It's best to visit this museum before deciding if you want to head out to the Terracotta Army excavation site. You can see the statues much much closer here and in comfort too.

The worst museum visiting experience I have ever had! I can book the ticket in advance but there are too many visitors inside and the air conditioning almost not function at all. It is crowded, hot and noisy. There are so many people push around to see the exhibits. Better to stay away from this museum.
Very nice museum with amazing historical relics. Much recommended if you are a fan of history.
They refuse to speak a single bit of English. The tickets are only through WeChat 5 days in advance. Horrendous place
Great museum to learn the history of China from the beginning to Tong dynasty. However, must visit around off hours or there are too many people

Absolutely difficult to book the ticket. It took me a few days to secure a booking due to system issues, but unfortunately, my gf wasn’t able to book due to her foreign passport. Simiarl to the situation in Xi'an Museaum, I ended up going on my own, and despite the large crowds, it was definitely worth the time.

This museum is a treasure trove of ancient Chinese artefacts. Beside the Terracotta Army excavation site, this is a must visit attraction in your Xi'an itinerary. There's a section where visitors can get a close-up viewing of the Terracotta soldiers and horses 🐎. Spend at least half-a-day in order to view other magnificent exhibits. Be there early and queue for your free entrance pass.
Countless artifacts from ancient Shaanxi and huge crowds to see them. Do not omit to visit the section with the wall and scroll paintings!
The treasures within make it worth the wait outside ! You will be connected to the Tang Dynasty, one of the most creative ones in China’s illustrious past.

Very good museum showing excavations from the four big dynasties (Zhou, Han, Sui, Tang) that had their capital in Xi'an. Very well preserved artifacts. Free entry with Chinese ID card or foreigners' passport.
wonderful experience travelling back to old times. so much to see, feel and discover yourself.

Could not book on WeChat as a foreigner. I went on trip app as advised by others on xiaohongshu and it wouldn’t allow me to book either. Apparently they allowed foreigners to book in past ( earlier in March it wasn’t an issue for my friend) but they don’t accept it any more. I recently travelled to other cities in China and had no issues booking museums on WeChat 小程序 with my passport, not sure why this one specifically doesn’t allow for it. I was told you had to go through a travel agency to purchase tickets but it’s also quite difficult if you don’t know of any local ones or if you plan to go the following day. The museum advises you call their hotline, but you can’t get through - the call drops after 30 seconds. The website link they posted for ticket purchases also doesn’t work.

The museum is not foreigner friendly. Warning: you need to book tickets in advance. For someone has no Chinese phone number or WeChat, plus their official English website booking page broke, it is impossible to book a ticket. I tried to explain at the ticket service but couldn't get the same day ticket. Best they could do is book one for me in three days.

Went on a Saturday morning without a reservation, counter staff said next available slots are 3 days later (Tuesday, it's closed on Mondays). I explained it's not possible to get a reservation without a local phone number, there was nothing she could do but to offer to help book for Tuesday. After that I found out that even locals have difficulty reserving tickets in advance on wechat. So I went to Xi'an museum instead, which gives a good overview of the history of Xi'an but artefacts are less impressive. Xi'an museum grounds are also nice and shady and has a small goose pagoda, and seem much less crowded.
3500 years history concentrate in this small museum but soon it will move to new one.

It’s so difficult for foreigners to not be able to book on site, only in some mini-App (in Chinese language), and it has to be in advance. I was in front of it, but not possible to visit, and I left Xi’An without visiting it… It’s very tiring for foreigners this system. I asked a friend to book for me in this Chinese mini-app, but it’s not allowed for foreigners to book there. Why discriminate foreigners?

1) Great Museum and book ahead before you go - need to bring ID etc. 2) Set time booking - so arrive at the agreed timing 3) Very busy even at a non holiday period - so expect crowds 4) When I went Oct 2023 - it was very warm inside building, no fans or aircon, so be prepared. Seating is only in the main entrance with the giant stone statue. 5) Dont walk the Xi'an City walls and then go straight to Museum - you will be very tired (lesson learnt)
Can't reserve tickets through mini program. It is not possible to input foreign passport. For foreigners, they scam you for 150 rmb on trip. Discrimination.
We were impressed by not only our guide's depth of knowledge, but by her absolute love of her museum and delight in sharing the stories of its artifacts.

Awesome museum. First it is free, though there would always be 30-meter line-up queue to get the free ticket. While you could buy a ticket for an extra exhibition entrance with 20yuan. It is real bargain to avoid the queuing. The collection is quite stunning . It took me almost 3 hours to visit around the museum. quite rewarding! One more thing, must rent an electronic guide, it would explain the exhibits in details.

Well worth visiting. Entry to most of the museum is free but you need to present a passport or ID card. One room required a ticket to be purchased but this needed to be done at the entrance where there was a queue. If I was going again or advising another visitor, I would say pay the fee (¥30) when you enter if you want to see everything.

The key draw, of course, is the abundance of artifacts, but that is hindered by the insanely long lines to get in for free, and the absence of a clear way to buy tickets so that you don't have to wait in line. Furthermore, the long lines translates into massive numbers of people inside so that you can get near many displays without a great deal of patience. Finally, the audio guide is only somewhat useful because the speaker has acceptable, but often incorrect English, the display numbers are sometimes out of any clear order, and the latter displays are completely missing, which is a huge time waster. There is a reasonable food court-style place to eat downstairs, albeit with just the one counter, but there is no cell reception and the wait can of course be long if you get the biǎng biǎng noodles, which aren't very good.

The ticket for the museum is free of charge, but you have to use the Chinese social media software WeChat to reserve it and a Chinese phone number to receive a confirmation code, than use the phone with the code to enter the museum. The process is CHINESE only. So, don’t waste your time for the free ticket, pay some money to the tourist guide around the museum let them bring you in.
One of the better museums I've encountered in China, with nicely designed lighting, and effective displays of a bewildering array of artefacts.

Crowded, very crowded even in a low season. It packs more people than British Museum in a single business day. Don't queues for the free tickets, there's no queues if you pay RMB30 for a ticket which also gives you access to paid sections in the museum.

With Bryan Bai private tour guide, obtaining tickets was a breeze. Once inside, his knowledge and enthusiasm made our exploration of the exhibits so much more interesting and informative. We could spend as much or as little time in any area as we chose. It's a very well laid out and fascinating museum.

Place where people just stuck at an item with their camera and not move anywhere. The only way to get in is to forcefully stepped in. Then you will have people complain why you force in. Extremely hot and stuffy inside.

Been here before.. there are times there are free tickets.. tourist doesn't need to queue up with the Chinese.. they have a special counters for tourists and the queue are usually much more shorter than the normal Chinese queue.. I been here once and the service counter was quite bad.. I can speak mandarin like other Chinese but sometimes I don't really understand their accents and I will usually asked a few times to make sure so this lady that I just uploaded the pictures was quite rude and gets frustrated after I asked a few times.. she doesn't seems to be very patience and almost shouted at me when the tickets runs out and asked me to purchase one.. in the end I didn't get the tickets and get in
As a foreign is impossible to buy tickets. You can only prebook on trip.com and during certain slots... These slots do not work!

Shaanxi History Museum is located in the northwest of the Xi’an Wild Goose Pagoda. It was built in 1983 and was open on June 20, 1991. Shaanxi History Museum is China’s first large-scale modern national museum; it marks that China’s museum career has entered into a new development mileage. The Museum has the style of Tang dynasty buildings of “central palace hall with four worship houses around” with orderly, harmonious, vigorous and grave construction, melting the national tradition, local characteristics and the spirit of time into an organic whole. The Museum covers an area of 65,000 square meters. It has a building area of 55,600 square meters, the cultural relic reservoir area of 8,000 square meters, and exhibition hall area of 11,000 square meters. Its collection of cultural relics reaches 370,000, dating from the simple stone that human used at the initial stage in ancient times down to all kinds implements in social life before 1840; the time span covers more than one million years. The cultural relics are rich in number and types and have high grade and wide value, among which Shang bronze is exquisite; terracotta figurines of past dynasties are of varied types and postures; gold and silver ware of Han and Tang Dynasty is unique across the country; wall paintings of Tang tomb have no equals in this world. It is called a collection of variety of boutiques carnival.
Excellent museum showcasing thousands of years of history in this province. It was incredibly hot inside on the day of my visit though; I think they should have a/c inside.

The Shaanxi Archaeology Museum, which features the history of archaeology and protection technologies, opened to the public in 2022. The museum is located in northwest China's Xi'an City, which has served as the capital of 13 dynasties. Home to the world-famous Terracotta Warriors, Xi'an is renowned for its rich cultural heritage resources. A total of 5,215 pieces of relics are on display at the Shaanxi Archaeology Museum, including a tombstone excavated with an epitaph written by Yan Zhenqing, one of the most renowned calligraphers in Chinese history. There is also a bronze chariot, dating from the Western Zhou Dynasty (1046 – 771 BC). The Shaanxi Archaeology Museum not only exhibits cultural relics, but also reproduces the process of the archaeology and restoration of cultural relics. It showcases the latest and most sophisticated archaeological technologies, and tells the stories of experts exploring the origin of Chinese civilization. "By showing the real scene of excavation, the museum aims to offer the public a closer look at archaeological research," said Sun Zhouyong, curator of the museum.

Fantasic musuem, full of really interesting stuff from around ShaanXi. Has a Terracotta Warriors sections complete with video (in Chinese). All the exhibits are well maintianed, however it can get really busy. There are 6000 free tickets available in the morning and 3000 in the afternoon. Its worth waiting for even if they say the museum is full- just wait 20-30 mins and the queue will move again. Or go to the Wild Goose which is about a 7 min walk away and come back later.

Ticket if free, but you need to have a long long Q. Suggest you going to the ticket counter to buy a ticket is only RMB 30. Totally no Q and you can straight away to go in. Inside very crowded and noisy. Worth to visit, can try to planning to stay around 4-5 hours here.

Nice modern museum. Too bad I arrived late so could only see 4 halls. Opening hours are not correct. Officially (mentioned on the ticket) open from 830 till 1800 from March till November but it was already closed at 5pm and entry only allowed until 4pm.

Buy a ticket or wait forever in queue. But don't expect to get an English digital tour audio guide, they say on their website that they have it but actually they don't. Very nice place but no fun without a guide.

Definitely worth a look if you feel like spending a few days in Xi'an. You can get a good understanding of the surrounding area and there are plenty of interesting artifacts. I would recommend spending at least two hours here, but come early to avoid the crowds

This is another must see sight in Xi'an. They have a huge collecting of relics and artefacts from the Tang Dynasty and they are spread out in numbers rooms to allow the guest to walk through time. It should be noted that the best room with the 'royal artefacts' requires you to pay an additional fee but it is not much and its worth seeing. You can get a Chinese (RMB 100) and English (RMB 150) tour guide which is worth doing as they do provide you with a lot more insight.

A fascinating collection of artifacts documenting Shaanxi history. I spent hours here touring the exhibits arranged in chronological order. If you go to see the terra-cotta warriors, a trip to this museum rounds out a historical appreciation of the area.

Not to be confused by the name as a "Shanxi" (equivalent to a state) level museum, it's a feast of the country history to your eyes, mind and soul. Prepare a whole entire day and for the feeling at the exit of entering a new world 宛如隔世

Can only reserve ticket online and tickets are always sold out weeks in advance. They says they have tickets that people returned at last minute, but marked up the price by a lot, I have hard time to believe that.
Buy a ticket and you won't regret! However, best to have a local friend to tell you some information about the things! Also be picky with the chosen time, can get crowded.
Amazing collection of artefacts here! If you're interested in history, this museum is a must-visit! Probably one of the most important and substantial collections in the nation.
We could not enter the museum because of the terrible non user-friendly reservation system.
Free entry with passport. When I visited, one hall would only admit people who had paid an extra ¥30 at the entrance.
Awesome museum. Need a bit luck to grab free tickets during the summer holiday. 😂
It contains thousands of precious historical remains and objects. A really good way to understand Chinese history, at least a part of it.
Lots of artwork, statues, jewelry, etc. If you are a history buff, this is a must. Includes some of the Terracotta Warriors.
Love the museum with it vast collection of artifacts. One of the best museum visited
It was really cool history and was cool to see the different objects found. It was really crowded and hard to take the time to really look.
You need to make reservations ahed of time and make sure you have your passport with you to gain entry.
Quality museum but the management is terrible. Expect to wait 2hours+ outside standing in line waiting for a ticket.
ummm, personally i see the items here to be a replicaa of some other museums in china. nothing new i think

在这块关中平原的土地下，埋藏着秦阿房宫、汉未央宫、隋大兴城、唐大明宫，又是丝绸之路的起点，数不尽的奇珍异宝，淋漓尽致的喷涌而出，所以说这是西安之行必须打卡之地！ 陕西历史博物馆国宝级文物就有18件，属中国博物馆前列。在网上预约了一个讲解人员，真的相当有必要。博物馆里面义务讲解很少，而且后面跟了好多好多人。网上预约的讲解员也不失专业性，全程下来两个半小时以上，真的能让人从多方面感受到文化丰富的内涵。 在博物馆内，连西汉“皇后之玺”玉印都属于一笔带过的那种。因为精彩纷呈的文物简直太多，许多在书上看到的文物，在此都能有展现。首当其冲，自然是秦彩绘跪射俑，听完讲解才知道俑出土的时候是有颜色的，而且精妙绝伦，不失装饰之感，出徒以后马上褪色。这也是为什么现在不开秦始皇陵原因之一。 总的来说，每个城市的博物馆都能体现其当地的文化价值与审美传承，对于长安这么一个有历史厚重感的城市来说，自然更是如此。只能说不虚此行。这是一场真真正正能够触摸历史文化的盛宴。
號稱十四朝古都的陝西，擁有最多秦、漢、唐等盛世王朝的出土文物，來此一遊絕對是對歷史文化的洗禮。 去年在成都博物館看展，雖然文物展品數量較多，但幾乎清一色都是墓葬品，而陝歷博除了豐富的墓葬品與陪葬品外，還有一般非墓葬品的古代文明器物展覽。 都說外行看熱鬧，內行看門道，強烈建議聘請解說人員介紹，官方的或外聘合格的都可以，才會讓你更沉浸其中。
非常難預約的博物館，因為免門票，所以參觀素質非常的不好。需要提前在館前排隊安檢進場。 首先人潮非常的多，館內並沒有明確的參訪人員管控、加上內部空調系統極為差勁，夏天前來簡直可以用悶熱災難來形容。 由於人潮擁擠，較難以好好靜態觀賞文物，強烈建議要找五人內的導覽解說，不然根本走馬看花。 然後堅真心建議真的不要夏天或寒暑假人潮高峰期前來，否則只會掃了興致。

地點特色：位於西安市中心，擁有非常大型的博物館，有七個展廳，從中國遠古到隋唐有不同年代的藏物展出，見證了不同年代的發展，展品非常多，短短幾個小時是無法逛完的，重點這是唯一一個博物館免費的，因此需要提前預約，非常重要。 活動體驗：如果單純看展品是沒有辦法深入了解，因此有兩個選擇1. 租電子導覽2. 排隊等導遊，兩個方法都可以，導遊速度快講重點，電子導覽則有將近400個文物說明。 推薦理由：一個博物館可以看到西安從古至今的展品，來一個抵多個，而且是免費的。

中国最重要的历史博物馆之一，拥有着丰富的馆藏文物，以西周，秦，西汉，和唐代的文物为主。非常值得参观，可惜门票很难预约，需要大家提前做好准备。另外陕西历史博物馆还新开了秦汉馆，同样可以免费预约参观。
予約が必要です。 決済はwechatpayのため、難しい場合は直接に博物館に行き予約をする必要があります。 7番の窓口にて予約できます。 パスポートが必要になりますので注意してください。 展示品は非常に多く中国の歴史を存分に学ぶことができます。 大抵の展示には英語の説明があります。（日本語はあまりありません） 17時過ぎには閉じるため、15:30～の入場の場合は気を付けましょう。

门票免费，但需要提前在官网或者微信公共账号上预约，并且只能预约三天之内的，名额有限，很难约到 “陕西历史博物馆”馆藏文物多达37万余件，从远古人类的简单石器，到1840年前社会生活中的各类器物，时间跨度长达一百多万年。 其中的商周青铜器精美绝伦，历代陶俑千姿百态，汉唐金银器独步全国，唐墓壁画举世无双。 博物馆浓缩了中华民族的历史精华，被誉为“华夏珍宝库”，是展示中国古代文明和陕西历史文化的艺术殿堂。
喜歡歷史或古蹟的朋友，一定要來這裡，絕對物超所值，事先要在網上預約門票，有時間段可以選擇，請提早進行，因為每天的門票數量有限，一下就滿了。 館藏陳列的寶物都非常精美，古人的手藝真的精采。看見兩千年前的文字與現在相同的感觸，讓我內心激動不已。傳承千年卻沒有在時間的長河中遺失，這真是太棒了。

這是一個擁有170萬件的珍貴博物館，共分成三個大展廳：基本陳設展（免費）、何家村窖藏展（30ＺＭＢ，可看基本陳設展）、唐代壁畫展（270ZMB，可看三館)，要提前一週用微信預約、付款，然後拿著手機預約成功的訊息排隊換票。避畫展連帶展出宋徽宗、閻立本、韓幹仿畫共四幅，非常珍貴。要仔細看完每一個館藏，需要很長時間，館內有餐飲部，提供餐食。如果有任何問題，可以到志工服務台去詢問，無論作品、參觀路線等，他們都很樂意解答。65隨以上敬老票是免費的，可以帶著證件排隊換票即可，不需要預約。

必需要於網上預約入場日子、時段。 網上預約， 每天早上10、11點，下午6、7點， 就是「放票」時間。 每個賬戶訂票上限5張。 我們訂了中午12:30-14:30進場。 館內區分了七個展覽廳。 1樓有1、2、3館 2樓有4、5館 地庫6、7館 館內資料豐富， 陳列出土的真品種類繁多。 以歷史時間作為展示次序， 從而去欣賞及了解中國歷史文化。 整體而言， 這個免費觀賞的博物館， 值得參觀。 仔細參觀時間， 建議預留至少兩小時。 唯獨是館內洗手間的衛生情況欠佳 有待改善。

精彩絕倫阿 不愧是經歷了13朝首都絲路的一個地方， 身為思路的起頭，充滿了文化與經濟發展的演變。從第一個展廳一開始到最後展廳，慢慢的詳細的用文物訴說每個改朝換代的一個故事。展出了各個時代不同的特色，除了生活上的用品，還有一些工藝的進步。最精彩的還是不同朝代的陪葬品， 具體呈現每個朝代不同的一個發展與君王的理念，讓原本的歷史課本上讀到的東西從平面的文字中活了起來。一定是一個絕具教育意義跟生活陶冶的一個好地方。每天有六千份免費的票，如果趕時間那就買票吧，值得！

陝西歷史博物館於1991年建成開幕，是中國第一個有現代化設施的大型國家級博物館。陝西歷史博物館是按照宮殿庭院式布局建造的高台及群體組合建築，佔地近7公頃，建築面積55,600平方米，博物館的常規展覽按照中國古代史的時間布展，分別在第一、二、三展廳，以周、秦、漢、唐四個朝代為重點，展示陝西歷史。第四、五展廳和東展廳設有專題展覽，不定期的更換主題。參觀歷史博物館是免費的，只要帶著身分證，外國人帶護照，台灣人帶台胞證，以證件換票即可。不過也因為如此，所以排隊隊伍很長。即使今天只是一般日的早上，不是假日，還是有看似要排至少半小時的隊伍。
